messages.subject: Formatting input
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I'm sorry if this is quite basic, but I'm fairly new to the field and so some of the ideas and terminology are lost on me still.
To generate the Wm and WM matrices from sequenza output, do you use the values from the mutations file output or the segments file output? 
For example, the segments output has the following headers;

"chromosome" "start.pos" "end.pos" "Bf" "N.BAF" "sd.BAF" "depth.ratio" "N.ratio" "sd.ratio" "CNt" "A" "B" "LPP"

With CNt being the estimated copy number of the tumour and A and B being the estimated number of their respective alleles. But the input shown in your example matrices on page 2 of the vignettes shows values up to 3 decimal places, how to you generate those values?

I think I'm missing something obvious, but I'm unsure. Any help would be appreciated

Cheers,
Lee Brannan

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Formatting input
parts:
Hi Lee,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy! How to generate and select CNA input is outlined here:

https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_input.md
https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_choice.md

We recommend using Falcon or Falcon-X to generate fractional copy number input as demonstrated in the toy example. Sequenza outputs integer-value copy numbers. This is akin to knowing the truth tumor phylogeny (the observed copy numbers should always be fractional due to subpopulation mixture) besides it often times has identifiability issue with regard to purity and ploidy.

Hope that this is helpful,
Yuchao
